passages.text: But tell me: how do you love your parents? If you do so with a constant regard for what is just, I join in your prayer; but if merely as it happens, I do not, for even on a small pretext you can become their enemies. If you love with knowledge, tell us what “parents” means. You will say, “Founders of a family line.” Why, then, have you not loved the origin of all things, if you have undertaken to do this with a just mind? But even now you will say, “We have not seen him.” Why, then, do you flatter insensible things without having searched? Even if it was difficult for you to know what God is, you could not fail to know what is not God, so that you might reason that God is not wood, not stone, not bronze, or anything else made of perishable matter.

lexical_decisions.rationale: γένος links the argument to lineage and parentage. Origin or source here refers to God; progenitor of all is a viable more explicitly personal alternative.
Retains the prayer compound; join in wishing this is also possible, rather than bare agreement.

passages.text: Were they not shaped by iron—and was not the iron that shaped them softened by fire—and is not fire itself extinguished by water? Does not water get its motion from wind, and does not wind have the origin of its movement from the God who made all things? For this is what the prophet Moses said: “In the beginning God made heaven and earth. But the earth was invisible and unformed, and darkness was over the abyss, and God’s Spirit was borne over the water.” And when God speaks, this Spirit, like his hand, fashions everything, separating light from darkness and spreading out the visible heaven after the invisible one, so that the regions above may be inhabited by the angels of light, while those below may be administered by the human being together with all things made for his sake.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸ δὲ ὕδωρ οὐχ ὑπὸ πνεύματος τὴν κίνησιν ἔχει
lexical_decisions.chosen: Does not water get its motion from wind
lexical_decisions.rationale: πνεῦμα can be wind or spirit. Wind fits the physical water-motion argument; the same word recurs as God’s Spirit in the quotation, preserving an important lexical link in these notes.
Here displacement or movement is intended, not religious ecstasy.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μετὰ τὸν ἀόρατον οὐρανὸν τὸν φαινόμενον ἐφαπλῶσαν
lexical_decisions.chosen: spreading out the visible heaven after the invisible one
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the visible/invisible distinction and after without supplying numbered heavens.

passages.text: For it was for you, the human being, that God commanded the water on the face of the earth to withdraw, so that the earth could offer you fruits. He made openings so that it might provide springs for you, streams of rivers might appear, and animals might be cast up. To put it briefly, so that everything could be at your service. Is it not for you that winds blow for the production of fruits, rains are brought, and seasonal turnings occur? Indeed, the sun and moon, together with the other stars, carry out their risings and settings for you, and rivers and lakes, together with all the springs, serve you. Therefore, just as greater honor was given to you, insensible though you are, so greater punishment through fire has been prepared for you in your ingratitude, because you were unwilling to know the one whom you ought to have known before all others.

lexical_decisions.rationale: Bored holes or passages; no modern geological mechanism is specified.

lexical_decisions.chosen: and animals might be cast up
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the casting-up image, not generic creation.
The turnings can concern the sun or seasons; the broader cyclical wording is retained.

passages.text: Even now, recognize from the lesser things the cause of all things, reasoning that water produces all things, that water receives its coming into being through the movement of spirit, and that spirit has its origin from the God of all. This is how you ought to reason, so that through reason you may be able to reach God, recognize your lineage, be born again through first-born water, and become an heir of the parents who begot you for incorruptibility.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸ δὲ ὕδωρ ὑπὸ πνεύματος κινήσεως τὴν γένεσιν λαμβάνει
lexical_decisions.chosen: water receives its coming into being through the movement of spirit
lexical_decisions.rationale: πνεῦμα can also be wind, as in 11.22. Spirit emphasizes its divine origin and the rebirth argument; physical wind remains a material alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: be born again through first-born water
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the unusual birth-wording. Primordial water is a contextual alternative but would conceal the explicit birth epithet.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῶν πρὸς ἀφθαρσίαν γεννησάντων σε γονέων
lexical_decisions.chosen: the parents who begot you for incorruptibility
lexical_decisions.rationale: The source has plural parents and does not identify them in this clause; neither a singular parent nor specific identities are substituted.

passages.text: Therefore come readily, like a son to a father, so that God may set down ignorance as the cause of your sins. But if, even after being called, you are unwilling or delay, you will perish by God’s just judgment, unwanted because you were unwilling. And do not imagine that if you become more reverent than all the reverent people who have ever existed, but remain unbaptized, you will ever be able to attain hope. For in this way you will rather undergo greater punishment, because you did not do good deeds in a good way. For doing good is good when it is done as God commanded. But if you are unwilling to be baptized as he determined, by serving your own will you are hostile to his purpose.

lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the repeated will-wordplay and passive rejection; not being willed because you did not will is more formally literal.

lexical_decisions.chosen: you did not do good deeds in a good way
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the distinction between good deeds and doing them well.
